result.note: Tested the dissolution of the Digital Communications Commission, the satellite spectrum allocation method and the longer validity of port green clearances.

questions.prompt: In September 2026, the Department of Telecommunications dissolved the Digital Communications Commission. Consider the following statements about this:
items: The Commission was an inter-ministerial body that reviewed telecom decisions.
Its functions were handed to a new panel of secretaries drawn from several ministries.
It was dissolved shortly after it had cleared terms for satellite spectrum.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the Commission was replaced by the telecom secretary alone, not by a multi-ministry panel. The dissolution came 18 days after the panel cleared satellite spectrum terms, leaving the auditor, the courts and Parliament as checks that act only after the fact.
questions.source: The Department of Telecommunications dissolved the Digital Communications Commission, the inter-ministerial body that reviewed telecom decisions, replacing it with the telecom secretary alone, 18 days after the panel cleared satellite spectrum terms.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the change to green clearances for ports made in September 2026:
items: The validity of port green clearances was raised to 30 years, with extensions permitted up to 40 years.
The change was notified by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: The validity was doubled to 20 years, with extensions to 30, and the change was made by the environment ministry, days after a shipping-secretary meeting pushed for it. Congress said the change is built for the Great Nicobar transshipment port.
questions.source: The environment ministry doubled the validity of port green clearances to 20 years, with extensions to 30, days after a shipping-secretary meeting pushed for exactly that.

questions.prompt: In September 2026, the Digital Communications Commission cleared terms for satellite spectrum. How was that spectrum allocated?
options: At a fixed revenue share without an auction
Through a sealed-bid auction among operators
Through a reverse auction on service tariffs
questions.explain: The satellite spectrum was allocated at a fixed revenue share rather than auctioned. The story notes this is the same method behind the 2008 2G scandal.
questions.source: That spectrum was allocated at a fixed revenue share rather than auctioned, the same method behind the 2008 2G scandal.
